title: Twins, Round by Round: Lanthanoids vs Actinoids
subject: Chemistry
objective: The two f-block rows below the periodic table (in line, it would be 32 columns wide) look like twins: both fill f orbitals, prefer +3 and contract across the row. But actinoid 5f lies close to 6d and 7s and extends further out, so actinoids reach +3 to +7 (lanthanoids never above +4), contract more, are more reactive, form more complexes and oxo ions such as UO₂²⁺, have more complex magnetism and lower early ionisation enthalpies. Every actinoid is radioactive; among the lanthanoids only promethium is.

tf.q: The actinoid contraction is smaller than the lanthanoid contraction.
Lanthanoids form linear oxo ions like UO₂²⁺.
Actinoids have a greater tendency to form complexes than lanthanoids.
The early actinoids have higher first ionisation enthalpies than the early lanthanoids.

ar.a: Assertion: Actinoids show a wider range of oxidation states. Reason: 5f, 6d and 7s are close in energy.
ar.r: Both true; the reason explains the assertion.

ar.a: Assertion: Lanthanoids reach +7. Reason: 4f electrons are easily removed.
ar.r: Both false: Ln stop at +4; 4f is buried.

mcq.q: Actinoids show more oxidation states because:
Which ion has no lanthanoid analogue?
Magnetic properties are more complex for:

mcq.explain: An combine with non-metals at moderate temperatures.

num.q: How many elements are in each series (Ce to Lu)?
How many f electrons does Am³⁺ have? (Am: [Rn] 5f⁷ 7s²)

short.q: Compare the oxidation states of lanthanoids and actinoids.
short.solution: Ln mainly +3 (+2, +4), never above +4; An +3 to +7 because 5f, 6d and 7s are close in energy.

short.q: Why do actinoids form complexes more readily?
short.solution: Their 5f orbitals extend further out and take more part in bonding.

short.q: Compare radioactivity in the two series.
short.solution: Among lanthanoids only promethium has no stable isotope; all actinoids are radioactive.

right: 5f, +3 to +7, larger contraction, all radioactive, more complexes
